messages.subject: osmar library conflict (openstreetmap parsing)
parts:
Hi,

As soon as I add/call the osmar library I get a conflict (try adding 'library(osmar)' to start of any server.R file):

The following object is masked from ‘package:utils’:

    find

Listening on http://...
Error in tags$hr : object of type 'closure' is not subsettable

It appears to be a conflict with the 'tags' as this is used in the osmar library as default for part the R osm data type after the raw .osm data has been processed into a R dataframe like structure.

I've tried to deal this conflict but none of the advice from stackoverflow seems to work. And i don't have any experience in dealing with conflicts of this type.

Can anyone help?

Bringing together shiny/rcharts/osmar will be really neat for geo analysis but this conflict is slowing the process down a little.

Thank you,

Tim

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: osmar library conflict (openstreetmap parsing)
parts:
Since osmar also has the tags object (as a function, or what R calls
"closure"), it overrides the tags object in shiny when you
library(osmar). The solution is to make sure you use the one in shiny
via shiny::tags$hr.

Please also note there may be other objects that are overridden by
osmar, such as `span` in geosphere, one of the dependencies of osmar.
When you see objects are masked by another package, you will have to
use package::object.

> library(shiny)
> library(osmar)
Loading required package: XML
Loading required package: RCurl
Loading required package: bitops
Loading required package: geosphere
Loading required package: sp

Attaching package: 'geosphere'

The following object is masked from 'package:shiny':

span


Attaching package: 'osmar'

The following object is masked from 'package:utils':

find

messages.author: 5f38782388823bb2
messages.subject: Re: osmar library conflict (openstreetmap parsing)
parts:
Many thanks for the help, that's clear it up.

In the meantime, I also used this fix for avoiding conflicting/masking packages by attaching and then detaching the osmar library within the shinyServer function - not sure this is the most efficient approach but seems to work:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
 
  datasetInput <- reactive({
    inFile <- input$file1
   
    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)
   
    library(osmar)
    osmDf <- get_osm(complete_file(), source = osmsource_file("dunbar.osm"))
    detach("package:osmar", unload=TRUE)

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: osmar library conflict (openstreetmap parsing)
parts:
If you only need the get_osm function from the osmar package, I'd
suggest you use osmar::get_osm(). This will avoid attaching the
package; only its namespace will be loaded, and the exported objects
in this package will not be visible in your workspace.

Regards,
Yihui
